text:
anne: Heads-up — RC.3 canary flagged by deploybot: SBOM provenance missing (no cosign signature) and vuln-scan found one moderate transitive CVE via a dev dependency. Canary is paused for eu-west-1.

deploy-bot: [auto] release rc.3 quarantined; canary halted. evidence: https://ci.redwood/reports/1738456789 (SBOM diff + vuln report).

chris: Anne — can you paste the artifact digest and exact vuln? want to confirm scope.

anne: artifact -> gcr.io/redwood/service-runtime:rc.3 @ sha256:0a1b2c3d4e5f
SBOM: cosign.sig missing for that digest
vuln: transitive -> fastparse v1.2.3 -> CVE-2024-9999 (moderate) introduced via build-tool dev dep. Not in our production deps, but shows up in SBOM generation.

liam: Two immediate options: 1) rollback EU canary to rc.2 (digest pinned) or 2) staged-unpublish of rc.3 in EU while we attach signatures + hotpatch. Which is lower risk?

marina: Legal/Compliance check — any regulatory problem with partly unpublishing artifacts in EU? @legal-bot can you advise?

legal-bot: [auto] For staged-unpublish in a region we require manager approval and an audit ticket. If rollback to a previously-signed artifact is possible, that is preferred. No automatic legal blocker for rollback.

chris: Ops prefers rollback to rc.2 for the eu canary, then run a targeted vuln scan. That avoids touching the artifact registry (no unpublish).

anne: I can trigger the rollback and rerun vuln scan. ETA ~12m. If scan passes we keep rc.2 pinned for EU and continue investigating rc.3 signing gap.

liam: Security preference: pin -> rollback -> open hotpatch PR to remove the transitive CVE from build-tooling. We should also ensure cosign signing step is enforced in the release pipeline so this doesn't recur.

marina: Plan agreed: 1) rollback EU canary -> rc.2 (pinned by digest) 2) rerun vuln scan for EU 3) attach cosign sig to rc.3 or rebuild+sign before any further rollout 4) open tracking ticket for hotpatch & pipeline watchdog. @chris can you run the rollback?

chris: Running now: `/deploy rollback --service=runtime --to-digest=sha256:9f8e7d6c5b4a --region=eu-west-1`

deploy-bot: [auto] rollback job started (#deploy-904). logs:
```
pulling image sha256:9f8e7d6c5b4a
updating service runtime (canary) in eu-west-1
switching 10% -> 0% rc.3, 0% -> 10% rc.2
```
status: in_progress

anne: Note: prefer not to unpublish any artifact to preserve reproducibility. Staged-unpublish only if rollback or pin fails.

legal-bot: Manual: if you decide to keep rc.3 unpublished longer than 24h, open compliance ticket and notify risk team. For rollback only, no further action required.

deploy-bot: [auto] rollback succeeded in eu-west-1 (#deploy-904) — final status: rc.2 pinned for canary.

chris: Reran vuln-scan on pinned rc.2 -> PASS (no fastparse exposure). Good to go for EU canary.

anne: I'll attach a cosign sig to rc.3 artifact and open PR for the hotpatch. Will also add a short note in release notes about the transient transitive CVE and that we pinned rc.2 in EU as a precaution.

marina: I'll set a 2-hour change window for the global retry after signatures are attached: 02:00-04:00 UTC. Notify release and compliance channels.

liam: Also file follow-up to enforce cosign step in CI: `CI-ops-371`. Security will add a periodic SBOM validation job.

anne: Thanks all. I'll update the release doc and close the loop once rc.3 is signed + hotpatch PR is merged. :thumbsup:
